extracted.intended_audience: advertisers, brand marketers, agency creatives, and industry readers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and implicit criteria for what makes Super Bowl commercials succeed or 'fumble', distilled from historical Big Game ad controversies and their outcomes. Useful for advertisers and agencies planning high‑profile broadcast spots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weigh creative risk against financial risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider both the creative risk and the financial risk when planning a Super Bowl spot; a Big Game slot is expensive and controversy is a high-stakes gamble.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece notes an $8 million+ price per slot and quotes Patti Williams that risks include financial and creative dimensions. Guidance: assess whether the potential buzz or memorability justifies the cost and potential negative fallout before greenlighting provocative creative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize positive impact, not just raw impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Brands want to be memorable and talked about, but ideally they should be remembered for positive impact rather than only for generating attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article cites marketers’ desire for memorable ads but warns that KPIs focused solely on 'impact' can lead to controversy without positive brand outcomes. Guidance: define KPIs that include sentiment and long‑term brand equity, not only reach or buzz.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-test creative with target consumers
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek feedback from core target consumers before airing high‑stakes work to gauge likely reactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Snickers' account references 'feedback from our target consumers has been positive' as part of the response. Guidance: include representative consumer testing to surface offensive or tone issues early and reduce risk of mass backlash.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid discriminatory, homophobic, or otherwise offensive humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not rely on humor or tropes that demean protected groups or that can be read as discriminatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Snickers' 'Mechanics' (2007) was called homophobic by advocacy groups and pulled. Guidance: run content through diversity/sensitivity review and outside stakeholders to catch harmful stereotypes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid insensitive portrayals of suicide and mental‑health issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Be extremely cautious when depicting suicide or self‑harm; such portrayals can be perceived as hurtful or triggering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GM's 'Robot' ad (2007) showed a robot jumping off a bridge and drew criticism from suicide‑prevention groups, prompting removal and reworking. Guidance: consult experts and perform sensitivity reviews for mental‑health content; have alternate edits ready.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match tone to the occasion — avoid morbid or 'buzzkill' messaging
rubrics_metrics.description: Super Bowl audiences expect entertainment; a spot perceived as morbid or depressing can generate negative reactions regardless of intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nationwide's 'Make Safe Happen' (2015) was criticized on social media as morbid and a buzzkill. Guidance: consider audience expectations for celebratory, light, or emotionally appropriate tone and ensure messaging fits the occasion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider animal‑welfare and ethical sourcing impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative that involves animals or animal purchase/sales should consider welfare concerns and how advocates may react.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GoDaddy's 'Journey Home' (2015) drew animal‑rights backlash over perceived encouragement of puppy mills and was pulled. Guidance: review portrayal of animals, sourcing implications, and likely activist responses; be prepared to respond or alter creative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid objectification and sexist portrayals
rubrics_metrics.description: Ads that objectify or marginalize women (or other groups) risk organized backlash and reputational harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carl's Jr.'s 'All Natural' (2015) was called out for objectifying women and sparked hashtags like #WomenAreMoreThanMeat. Guidance: evaluate portrayals for sexism, test with diverse audiences, and anticipate organized responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious with polarizing political or immigration messaging
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly political or immigration‑focused creative can generate sharply divided reactions and may be rejected by broadcasters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 84 Lumber's 'The Entire Journey' (2017) confronted immigration and had its original ad rejected by Fox, leading to a revised version and driving viewers to the brand site for the ending. Guidance: assess political risk, platform acceptance, and whether the brand wants to be aligned with a particular stance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check sponsor/organizational credibility and affiliation risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that the sponsor's prior affiliations or organizational ties do not undermine the ad's message or expose the campaign to hypocrisy claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: He Gets Us' 2023 ads were criticized because the foundation had ties to a group with controversial stances, prompting accusations of hypocrisy. Guidance: vet sponsoring organizations and anticipate how past affiliations may be used to critique the ad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect personal and family sensitivities when using likenesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Using real individuals' images or family members in political or sensitive messaging can provoke personal backlash and public apology requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: American Values 2024's RFK Jr. ad upset family members who felt their likenesses were used inappropriately; RFK Jr. apologized. Guidance: obtain clear permissions, consider family sentiments, and weigh reputational tradeoffs when using public figures' images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure compliance with broadcaster and platform standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Broadcasters and platforms may reject or demand edits to spots they deem too controversial or noncompliant with their policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fox rejected 84 Lumber's original imagery; the NFL 'nixed' the Cardi B NYX ad requiring last‑minute changes. Guidance: confirm content compliance with intended broadcasters, secure approvals in advance, and have alternate cuts prepared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have contingency plans for edits, removals, or shortened versions
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare for the possibility that an ad will be pulled, shortened, or moved online only; plan alternative executions and call‑to‑action routes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include Snickers and GoDaddy removing ads from TV and YouTube, GM reworking an ending, and NYX shortening its spot and adding a QR to the full version. Guidance: create contingency edits, digital fallbacks, and clear PR lines to implement quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate social media backlash and organize a PR response strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: High‑visibility ads will be scrutinized on social platforms; brands should anticipate negative posts, petitions, and media coverage and have a rapid response plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple cases in the article show viral social reaction (petitions for GoDaddy, hashtags for Carl's Jr., critical posts about Nationwide). Guidance: prepare messaging, spokespeople, and escalation paths before airing; monitor reactions in real time and respond transparently.
